problem_statement: nisarhassan12/portfolio-template is a static single-page developer portfolio (index.html + index.css + index.js, no build step) for Rowan Ashcroft, an embedded firmware & IoT engineer: a hero header, a 'My Work' section of three project cards, a Clients logo row, an About section, and a Contact footer. The owner is adding a 'project intake flow' so visitors understand how work is taken on, organised by the four intake stages Scope / Prototype / Field-test / Handover. The 'My Work' section opens with an intake summary strip of four metric tiles (Projects intook, Firmware builds, Field deployments, Handover docs) and a discipline filter (All work / Firmware / Hardware / Fieldwork). Deliver three coordinated things while preserving the dark pink-accent Rowan visual system: (1) REPAIR the intake metric strip so it stays within the viewport on a 390px phone with no horizontal overflow (the original strip is a fixed 760px non-wrapping row that pushes the whole page sideways); do not merely clip it with overflow-x:hidden — the document itself must not exceed the mobile viewport width. (2) Promote the intake-stage taxonomy into a shared 'Intake stages' rail that appears consistently in the work section, the about section AND the footer, styled to match the dark Rowan editorial language (near-black panel, pink accent border/title, off-white stage chips, 8px radius) — the rendered rail must be visually faithful to the reference, not a collapsed or off-palette light slab. (3) Wire the work-section discipline filter end to end: clicking a filter button (Firmware / Hardware / Fieldwork / All work) must update the '#intake-readout' readout to 'Showing: <selected discipline>' in addition to highlighting the active button — the post-click terminal state must reflect the selection, not the default. Keep the hero header, the three project cards with their tech lists, the Clients row, the About bio, the Contact block, the footer social links, scripts, and desktop/tablet layout intact.
required_content: The intake metric strip keeps its four tiles (Projects intook, Firmware builds, Field deployments, Handover docs) unchanged in text and order, and renders within the viewport on a 390px phone with no horizontal document overflow beyond 24px.

A shared 'Intake stages' rail (Scope / Prototype / Field-test / Handover) appears consistently in the work section, the about section AND the footer — the same intake component in all three places, not only next to the work metric strip.

The 'Intake stages' rail keeps the dark Rowan editorial look (near-black panel, pink accent border/title, off-white stage chips, 8px radius) and is visually faithful to the reference rendering — not a collapsed or off-palette light restyle.

The work-section discipline filter is wired end to end: clicking a filter button updates the '#intake-readout' readout to 'Showing: <selected discipline>' (e.g. clicking Firmware sets 'Showing: Firmware') in addition to marking the button active; the post-click terminal state reflects the selection, not the default 'Showing: All work'.
The desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts stay within their viewports.

The hero header, the three project cards with their tech lists, the Clients logo row, the About bio, the Contact block, and the footer social links remain reachable and unchanged, and the static site keeps a clean browser console (no remote CDN/font errors).
design_constraints: Fix the responsive layout of the intake metric strip; do not delete the strip, change its four tiles, or restyle unrelated sections.
Add the SAME shared 'Intake stages' rail component to the work, about and footer sections so the intake-stage language is consistent site-wide; do not add it to only one section.

Preserve the Rowan design language: black background, pink (#ff3258) accent, off-white text, rounded 8px cards, uppercase section headings; the rail must render in the dark pink-accent palette, not an inverted light slab.
Keep the discipline filter interaction wired end to end (the #intake-readout terminal readout must reflect the clicked discipline), not merely a class toggle.
Do not introduce external stylesheets, remote fonts, CDNs, or new remote script/asset dependencies; the site must stay a self-contained static site with a clean console.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial protect the rebranded header hero, nav, background treatment, CTA, and static first-view behaviour across viewports.
desktop_work_regression and mobile_work_regression scroll to #work and verify the three rebranded project cards render and stay responsive.
desktop_clients_regression protects the logo strip after the rebrand.
desktop_about_regression protects the rebranded About Me bio, resume button, and profile image.
desktop_contact_regression protects the rebranded Get in Touch copy and the persona email link.
desktop_footer_regression protects the footer social icons, credit text, and back-to-top link.

Baseline captures should still complete because the original #work, #clients, #about, #contact, and .footer targets exist; the demo persona, demo project cards, and Lorem-ipsum copy should be scored as missing completion / visible text and as forbidden residue, not as capture failure.

change_completion: The intake metric strip renders its four tiles within the viewport on mobile.
The shared 'Intake stages' rail appears in the work, about and footer sections.
The discipline filter click updates the #intake-readout terminal readout to the selection.
design_consistency: The Rowan palette, card chrome, accent color, and section rhythm are preserved.
The 'Intake stages' rail keeps the dark pink-accent look and is visually faithful to the reference across the three sections.
interaction_continuity: Clicking a filter button updates the 'Showing:' readout to the selected discipline (post-click terminal state reflects the change, not the default).
regression: Hero header, project cards, clients row, about bio, contact and footer remain reachable and unchanged.
The static site serves from index.html with a clean browser console.
responsive: 390px homepage (initial, work strip, footer) and 834px tablet have no horizontal overflow beyond 24px.
The metric tiles wrap or shrink cleanly instead of forcing a fixed-width row.

scoring_notes: A correct patch is a coherent implementation-continuity rebrand of the whole portfolio into one fictional developer using the existing static HTML / CSS / vanilla-JS files, preserving the section structure, nav, local assets, and static serving. Leaving the demo persona, demo project cards, or Lorem-ipsum copy in any section, or only rebranding the hero, should not pass.

metadata.design_goal: fit the repo architecture, component boundaries, build system, and source conventions
metadata.selected_repo_reason: nisarhassan12/portfolio-template is a runnable static developer portfolio with clear Work, Clients, About, and Contact sections, real local project/client/profile assets, one CSS file, one vanilla JS file, and no build step, making it a natural L2 portfolio implementation-continuity rebrand task.

author_notes: Repo-grounded static-portfolio modify/flow task hardened to L4. The reference (a) repairs the intake metric strip mobile overflow (fixed 760px nowrap -> wrapping flex 1 1 140px), (b) promotes a shared 'Intake stages' rail into the work, about and footer sections in the dark pink-accent Rowan palette, and (c) wires the discipline filter so #intake-readout reflects the clicked discipline. The bad 'smart-wrong' solution narrows the strip to 560px + overflow-x:hidden (still overflows -> D6 fail), adds the rail to the work section only (D2 cross-section fail on about + footer), restyles the rail into an off-palette light slab (D3 visual_regression fail), and toggles the filter's .active class without re-syncing #intake-readout (click succeeds but the terminal readout stays 'Showing: All work' -> D4 interaction_assertions fail). It fails FOUR distinct gates while all text/completion/regression/console signals pass. body{overflow-x:hidden} was neutralized to overflow-x:visible as declared INFRA identical across all legs so the mobile overflow is measurable.
